stem.text: Ethanedioic acid, $\text{HO}_2\text{CCO}_2\text{H}$, can be oxidised by $\text{KMnO}_4$ in dilute sulfuric acid. The products of this reaction are carbon dioxide, water, potassium sulfate and manganese(II) sulfate.
In this reaction each ethanedioic acid molecule loses two electrons as it is oxidised. A half-equation for this process is shown.
How many water molecules are produced when five ethanedioic acid molecules are oxidised by $\text{KMnO}_4$ in dilute sulfuric acid?
